NSWindow.globalFrameOnOtherScreenLandsOn.notes: AppKit re-places a window created with a global frame on another screen onto the main screen: the screen: initialiser is required.

StageManager.doesNotReachAVirtualDisplay.notes: A window adopted onto a virtual display keeps its whole frame: no window has ever been observed thumbnailed there, on any run, while five applications were thumbnailed at once on the physical display in the same session. This is a property the seat depends on rather than one it arranges, and every Command rests on it: a point is computed from the window server's frame, so a thumbnail would put the point outside the control. The oracle is the Live input matrix, which refuses to post anything unless the adopted window reads full size inside the display's bounds, so a build where this stopped holding would fail every row instead of landing events in the wrong place.

StageManager.stashesInactiveWindowsToThu.notes: Stage Manager stashes inactive windows down to a thumbnail in its strip, so a routed event reaches the process but lands outside the control. This is why a window is staged before a Command. Observed on 09/09/2026 with Stage Manager on: five inactive applications thumbnailed at once on the physical display, 136x187 and the like, in the strip at x=15, each paired with a WindowManager window. Two things it does NOT do, both measured: it does not stash on a schedule or by policy, only as a consequence of another application being activated, which is why a driver that never activates anything cannot cause a stash and cannot time the un-stashing; and no window has ever been observed stashed on a virtual display, which is where an adopted window sits.

CALayer.contentsAcceptsIOSurface.notes: The zero-copy Monitor stands on it: CALayer.h says contents may be an IOSurfaceRef, the web documentation lists only CGImage and NSImage. Both the ObjC IOSurface and the CF IOSurfaceRef are accepted, and the round trip through CVPixelBufferGetIOSurface is the form ScreenCaptureKit delivers. A unit test in SeatCaptureTests assigns a real surface to a MonitorLayer, so the day the header stops being true a test says so.

SCStreamConfiguration.defaultsDifferFrom.notes: Real defaults are minimumFrameInterval 1/60, queueDepth 8, pixelFormat 420v, all different from the public documentation: the kit sets all three explicitly.
